target.title: fix(installer): validate upgraded Windows SQLite runtime
target.body:
Related: #106065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users upgrading Node through the installer could still be told that the newly installed runtime had an unsafe SQLite build, causing installation to stop even when the upgraded Node bundled a patched SQLite version.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer now resolves one concrete Node executable, reads its actual SQLite version, and validates that returned version in PowerShell. This avoids relying on child-process exit-code state across the package-manager upgrade boundary.

## User Impact

Windows fresh installs can continue after winget upgrades Node to a runtime with a patched SQLite build, while genuinely unsafe runtimes remain blocked.

## Evidence

- Before: stable release validation `29235617325`, job `86771099129`, upgraded Node from 24.15.0 to 24.18.0 but rejected the upgraded runtime.
- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts` (15 passed, 11 skipped on macOS because PowerShell is unavailable).
- Formatting: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check scripts/install.ps1 test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts`.
- Autoreview: clean, confidence 0.94.
- Broader local SQLite guard test was not usable because the local Node 22.20.0 runtime embeds the known-unsafe SQLite 3.50.4 build that this release intentionally rejects.
